description: Four Rust crates: lgwks_std, a zero-config stand-in for a dozen crates; lgwks_bot, a capability-gated runtime; lgwks_deps, the storefront that owns every edge; lgwks_ast, a standalone parser.
rules: Prefer lgwks_std over a third-party crate for anything it provides: encoding (base64, percent-encoding), fs traversal, glob, hex, leb128, hashing, JSON, RON, regex, retry budgets, single-threaded task execution, timestamps, UUIDs, HTTP, and tracing.

Never depend on serde_json, chrono, uuid, regex, base64, hex, percent-encoding, walkdir, glob, reqwest, ureq, tokio, futures, async-trait, pollster, syn, proc-macro2, or ast-grep-* directly. Each names a workspace path that already wraps it.

Async, timers, channels, and runners come from lgwks_bot. Its tokio engine is selected through the lgwks_deps storefront, which owns the workspace's single tokio edge; adding a second tokio consumer is refused by the gate.

Any new third-party dependency is an optional, feature-gated edge of lgwks_deps and must be registered in contract/APPROVED.toml. Do not introduce a new owner crate or a new top-level crate for third-party code.
lgwks_bot executes exactly four verbs: Observe, Evaluate, Execute, Query. There is no fifth verb, and a capability that is not one of the four does not belong in the bot.

Observe::fingerprint is opt-in and defaults to None, which polls every tick exactly as before. A source that can answer "has this moved?" from a key it already holds — an ETag, an mtime, a row version, a mutation counter — returns Some(u128).

When a source returns Some(fingerprint), the tick never calls poll and never constructs the value. The contract is exact: equal fingerprints must imply equal values, or the substrate skips a real movement silently.
Return None from Observe::fingerprint when producing the digest would cost a round trip, or when the key is not a faithful function of the value.

Authority in lgwks_bot is proof-carrying. Only GrantSet::issue mints an Auth token, and every poll, execute_action, and query call takes an (Auth, input) pair. Evaluate takes no proof because it is pure.
Build bots with Bot::builder(name).observe(source).on(condition, action), ending in build(&grants).
observe does not erase: the source stays a concrete S, so on types its condition and action against S::Output, and a mismatched chain fails to compile rather than at runtime.
A spec's strings resolve through the DomainRegistry a binary declares with domains!, and an identifier outside that list is refused with BotError::UnregisteredDomain naming it.
BotSpec is validate-only: no from_spec materializer exists yet. ChainSpec::on is a bare identifier with no slot for a condition's parameters such as Above<u16>'s threshold.
The second obstacle to a from_spec materializer: an erased source carries no durable statement of its Output type.
Use tracing for diagnostics. println! and eprintln! are forbidden in library code, and library code must not unwrap or expect on recoverable paths — return typed errors with ?.

A domain that fails returns BotError::DomainError { domain, certainty, cause }. The certainty: DispatchCertainty field is required: Refused means nothing was dispatched and nothing ever will be, NotDelivered means nothing reached the peer.

Unsettled means it may have taken effect, so a retry is a possible duplicate. BotError::retry_class() reads it — Never, Safe, RequiresEvidence. State what the failure actually establishes; never parse a cause string to decide whether to retry.

lgwks_ast is standalone and finished, not grandfathered and not awaiting work. Do not grow it into a fourth dependency surface, do not route it through lgwks_deps, and do not propose capability additions to it.
Licences differ by crate and are load-bearing: lgwks_bot is MPL-2.0, file-level copyleft, while lgwks_std, lgwks_ast and lgwks_deps are Apache-2.0, and the repository root is MPL-2.0.
The LICENSE file in a crate's own directory governs that crate; LICENSING.md states the model, the commercial option, and why lgwks_bot is closed to outside contributions until a CLA exists.
